solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: At last, floor space charge generates profit (6)

indicatorNotes.At last: each of the next words gives up its final letter

blocks.note: a ward is a young person in someone's charge

annotation.surface: A landlord makes money by renting out floor space.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Floor space charge' reads as one rental fee; it splits into two letter sources and a separate noun, with 'charge' meaning a person looked after.
annotation.definitionFit: A reward is a gain or benefit, which is what profit is in its looser sense.

entries.clue: Building problem — slope flanking siding unstable (6,4)

indicatorNotes.flanking: the slope sits on both sides of the other letters
indicatorNotes.unstable: the letters of siding are not fixed in order

annotation.surface: A builder reports a problem: a bank of earth beside a railway siding has become unstable.
annotation.walkthrough: Rising damp is moisture drawn up from the ground into the walls of a building, a familiar complaint in older British houses.
annotation.definitionFit: Rising damp is a defect in a building's fabric, so a building problem.

entries.clue: Cheer TV doctor overseeing surgical procedure (5)

indicatorNotes.overseeing: in a down clue, the first part sits above the second

blocks.note: Doctor Who, the BBC time traveller

annotation.surface: A television doctor supervises an operation and there is cause for celebration.
annotation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC science-fiction series; in crosswords 'TV doctor' almost always means WHO.
annotation.definitionFit: To whoop is to give a loud cry of joy, which is to cheer.

entries.clue: Abusively criticised bloody despicable cuts (7)

indicatorNotes.cuts: one word cuts into the other, splitting it

blocks.note: vile = despicable; it goes inside RE…D

annotation.surface: Someone was savagely attacked in print for making despicable cuts, perhaps to public spending.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' looks like spending cuts, the thing criticised; it is the instruction for VILE to cut into RED.
annotation.definitionFit: To revile someone is to criticise them in abusive language.

entries.clue: Vulgar scheme involves English bishop that is retiring (8)

indicatorNotes.involves: the scheme takes the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.retiring: going backwards, as one retires by withdrawing

blocks.note: IE (id est, that is) turned round

annotation.surface: A crude plot is uncovered in which an English bishop is quietly stepping down.
annotation.walkthrough: IE is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'; 'retiring' reverses it, since to retire is to draw back.
annotation.definitionFit: Plebeian means coarse or common, of the lower orders, which is what vulgar means.

entries.clue: Uncovered definitive sweet or savoury drink (5)

indicatorNotes.Uncovered: with its outer covering stripped off, first and last letters go

blocks.note: CLASSIC without its outer C and C

annotation.surface: A menu promises the ultimate drink, available sweet or savoury.
annotation.walkthrough: A lassi is a South Asian yoghurt drink, served sweet (often with mango) or salted.
annotation.definitionFit: A lassi comes in both sweet and savoury versions, so the description fits exactly.

entries.clue: Unsound victory buries Liberal prime minister (7)

indicatorNotes.buries: the Liberal is put inside, as a body is put in the ground

blocks.note: bad = unsound, as in bad reasoning

annotation.surface: A dubious election win sees a Liberal prime minister buried politically.
annotation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was a Conservative prime minister three times between the wars; 'Liberal' in the surface points to the wrong party.
annotation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin served as British prime minister in the 1920s and 1930s.

entries.clue: Break tile under base (9)

indicatorNotes.base: base means debased or corrupted, so the letters are corrupted into a new order

annotation.surface: A tile has cracked underneath, at the base of something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like the instruction to scramble; it is the definition, and the unusual indicator is 'base', in the sense of debased.
annotation.definitionFit: An interlude is an interval or pause, a break between parts of something.

entries.clue: New sign put up when Santa comes (4)

indicatorNotes.put up: in a down clue, raised so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: LEO, a sign of the zodiac, turned upward

annotation.surface: A new sign is put up to announce Father Christmas's arrival.
annotation.walkthrough: LEO is one of the twelve zodiac signs; in a down clue 'put up' makes it read upward.
annotation.definitionFit: Noël is French for Christmas, used in English carols, and Christmas Eve is the night Santa arrives.

entries.clue: Made anxious under previous religious office (8)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, this part comes below the next

annotation.surface: Someone is fretting over a church post they held before.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Made anxious' gives ATE through the idiom 'what's eating you?', meaning what is worrying you.
annotation.definitionFit: A priorate is the office or term of a prior in a religious house.

entries.clue: Awful slurs — I vow this will eventually plague host (4,5)

indicatorNotes.Awful: the letters are in an awful mess

annotation.surface: Someone who has been insulted swears the insults will come back to haunt the person who hosted them.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive rather than a synonym: a slow virus lies dormant a long time before attacking its host.
annotation.definitionFit: A slow virus has a long incubation, so it only eventually makes its host ill.

entries.clue: Turner and others reflecting about what gets him going (5)

indicatorNotes.reflecting: turned back as in a mirror
indicatorNotes.going: what gets something going is its start, the first letter

blocks.note: ET AL (and others) turned round, split around H

annotation.surface: The painter Turner and his circle look back on what inspired him.
annotation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter J M W Turner; it is a machine that turns wood or metal.
annotation.definitionFit: A lathe turns the workpiece while it is shaped, so it is a turner.

entries.clue: Protracted campaigns can now polarise careers (10,4)

indicatorNotes.careers: to career is to rush about wildly

annotation.surface: Drawn-out political campaigns can now split people's working lives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Careers' reads as a noun; it is a verb, to career, and it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: The Napoleonic Wars ran from 1803 to 1815, a long series of military campaigns.

entries.clue: Sinister individual abandoned description of her? (4-6)

blocks.note: the word HER spelt out as 'H and ER'

annotation.surface: A menacing man walks out on a woman, and here is what she looks like.
annotation.walkthrough: Sinister is Latin for left, and heraldry still uses it for the left side; so a sinister individual is left-handed, not wicked.
annotation.definitionFit: Sinister means on the left, so a sinister person is one who favours the left hand.

entries.clue: Psalmist prepared seventeenth-century bible lines (5)

indicatorNotes.lines: one word lines the other, wrapping round it

blocks.note: did = prepared, as in 'did the vegetables'
the Authorised Version of 1611, set inside D…ID

annotation.surface: The writer of the psalms drafts verses for the King James Bible.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lines' looks like the verses of scripture; it is the verb, with DID lining the AV.
annotation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms.

entries.clue: City in which you must be protected by vehicle insurance (9)

indicatorNotes.must be protected by: the letters are sheltered inside the insurance word

blocks.note: U = you in text-speak, placed inside CO…VER

annotation.surface: A city where drivers are legally required to have motor insurance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You' becomes U as in text messages, and it is the one protected, sitting inside the insurance.
annotation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a city in British Columbia, Canada.

entries.clue: Risky undertaking, coming by river (9)

indicatorNotes.by: one part set beside the next

blocks.note: an advent is an arrival, a coming
the Ure, a river in Yorkshire

annotation.surface: A daring enterprise arrives by way of a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river that crosswords use constantly; 'coming' is a noun here, an arrival.
annotation.definitionFit: An adventure is a bold undertaking with an uncertain, risky outcome.

entries.clue: Test 1960s car model — very old Mercedes, essentially (4,4)

indicatorNotes.essentially: take the essence, the letters at the heart of the word

blocks.note: the Vauxhall Viva, a British family car launched in 1963
the two middle letters of merCEdes

annotation.surface: A road test pits a 1960s saloon against a vintage Mercedes.
annotation.walkthrough: The Vauxhall Viva was a British family car of the 1960s; 'essentially' takes the heart of Mercedes.
annotation.definitionFit: A viva voce is an oral examination, a test conducted by spoken questions.

entries.clue: Table designer’s almost repaired exposed tube (9)

indicatorNotes.almost: stop one letter short of the end

blocks.note: a sleeve is a tube; SLEEVE without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A furniture maker's nearly finished repair to a table leaves a pipe showing.
annotation.walkthrough: The table is not furniture but the periodic table, which Dmitri Mendeleev drew up in 1869.
annotation.definitionFit: Mendeleev devised the periodic table of the elements.

entries.clue: Plant centre in New Guinea flourishing (7)

indicatorNotes.centre in: take the letter at the centre of the word
indicatorNotes.flourishing: the letters are waved about into a new order

annotation.surface: A plant nursery in New Guinea is doing well.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New Guinea' reads as one place name; it splits, with only the centre of 'New' kept.
annotation.definitionFit: Eugenia is a genus of tropical shrubs and trees in the myrtle family.

entries.clue: Remained twisted, tense and obscene (5)

indicatorNotes.twisted: the letters are twisted out of order

annotation.surface: Someone stayed on, warped, on edge and foul-mouthed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twisted, tense and obscene' reads as three adjectives in a row; the first is the instruction, the other two supply the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Dwelt is a past tense of dwell, to stay or remain.

entries.clue: Rescue one that’s been crushed by digger (7)

indicatorNotes.that’s been crushed by: the one is squeezed inside the digger

annotation.surface: A rescue is mounted for someone crushed by an excavator.
annotation.walkthrough: A delver is one who delves, an old word for a digger; 'one' is I, as the Roman numeral.
annotation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to rescue them, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

entries.clue: Brief stint to improve football club before unlimited team growth (14)

indicatorNotes.Brief: cut short by its last letter
indicatorNotes.before: this part comes ahead of the next
indicatorNotes.unlimited: without its limits, the first and last letters

blocks.note: a bout is a stint; BOUT cut short
to gain is to improve, as in gain strength
Aston Villa, the Birmingham football club

annotation.surface: A short spell of coaching to lift a football club ahead of unrestricted squad expansion.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word reads as football management; 'growth' at the end looks like the club's ambition and is in fact a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: Bougainvillaea is a climbing tropical shrub, and a plant is a growth.

entries.clue: Partly explain remark legally directed against property (2,3)

indicatorNotes.Partly: the answer is part of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A lawyer offers a partial explanation of a comment about property.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between two words; 'legally' signals that it is a Latin legal phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: In rem is the legal Latin for an action against a thing, such as property, rather than a person.

entries.clue: Pointer litter abandoned by female (5)

indicatorNotes.abandoned by: the female letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a farrow is a litter of pigs
F = female, the letter that leaves the litter word

annotation.surface: A pointer dog's litter of puppies has been abandoned by their mother.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' and 'litter' together suggest a gun dog and her pups; the pointer is an arrow and the litter belongs to a pig.
annotation.definitionFit: An arrow is a sign that points the way.

entries.clue: Caught male with female cook (4)

indicatorNotes.with: the parts go together side by side

annotation.surface: A man is caught in the act with a woman cook.
annotation.walkthrough: C for caught is from cricket scorecards; 'female cook' reads as one unit but splits after 'female'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: chef is the French word for a head cook, now used for any professional cook.

entries.clue: Safe place to receive focus of attention (5)

indicatorNotes.focus of: the focus is the centre point, the middle letter

blocks.note: to have is to receive, as in 'have a letter'
the middle letter of attENtion's nine

annotation.surface: A secure spot where one can get the attention one needs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Focus of attention' reads as the centre of interest; here it is literally the centre letter of 'attention'.
annotation.definitionFit: A haven was originally a harbour, where ships shelter from storms, hence any safe place.

entries.clue: Grass company really cutting back parts obtained from waste (9)

indicatorNotes.cutting: the letters cut into the grass word
indicatorNotes.back: the rear letter is cut off

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
VERY without its last letter; CO and VER go inside RE…ED

annotation.surface: A company informer drastically trims spending on waste-derived parts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the verb to inform on someone; it is the plant. 'Cutting back' is two jobs, a container and a shortening.
annotation.definitionFit: Recovered materials are salvaged from waste for reuse.

entries.clue: Weapons companies checking defaced equipment (8)

indicatorNotes.checking: holding back, keeping the other letters within
indicatorNotes.defaced: its face, the first letter, removed

blocks.note: GEAR without its first letter, inside FIR…MS

annotation.surface: Arms companies inspect vandalised kit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Defaced' means the face, or first letter, of GEAR is removed; 'checking' means holding in, as in checking an advance.
annotation.definitionFit: Guns, rifles and pistols are all firearms, one class of weapons.

entries.clue: Artist’s back pay for services rendered (6)

indicatorNotes.back: 'back' as in going back: the payment word is read from its back end to its front

blocks.note: a reward is payment for service, and the answer to 1 across

annotation.surface: A painter's back pay for work done.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Artist's back pay' reads as money owed to a painter; the 's is 'is', and 'back' turns the payment round.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-favoured sense: one who draws pictures, alongside the everyday drawer of a desk.
